transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Mateo Cruz (Redwood) - Rachel Kim, Alex Moreno, Samir Patel, Leah Chen (Seabright)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, I'll run through the agenda quick, uh, introductions, goals for the pilot, security, then Priya will walk through the technical plan.
[00:15] Rachel Kim: Thanks Jordan, Rachel here, CTO at Seabright. We're excited to get this rolling. Primary goals are faster triage of patient intake notes and a secure, HIPAA-conscious deployment.
[00:29] Alex Moreno: Alex - Head of Data. We'll provide sample production-ish payloads, and want to measure latency and token cost.
[00:40] Samir Patel: Samir, InfoSec. I'll be focused on SSO, audit logs, KMS, and where data resides.
[00:50] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda: 1) what success looks like for Seabright, 2) security and compliance checklist, 3) pilot scope and timeline, 4) next steps.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya, Solutions Engineer. I'll outline the pilot architecture: we usually recommend dedicated capacity for predictable latency, but hosted can work for early validation. We'll propose a small dedicated pool for the pilot.
[01:20] Leah Chen: Quick question — what's the minimum throughput you can guarantee for a pilot? We have spikes during morning intake.
[01:28] Priya Nair: So for dedicated, we size GPUs to target your SLOs, e.g., p99 latency < 300ms for short prompts. For larger prompts (300-800 tokens) p95 is more typical. We also use batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost while keeping tail latency low.
[01:50] Alex Moreno: When you say caching, is that off by default? Is it safe for PHI?
[01:57] Priya Nair: Good callout. Cache is configurable; for PHI we recommend disabling persistent shared cache or using per-customer isolated KV with encryption. It can also be set to TTL=0 for strict safety.
[02:12] Samir Patel: And encryption—KMS or HSM options? We require customer-managed keys.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: Yes, we offer KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys for private deployments. For Dedicated we can enable bring-your-own-key. We'll send the security supplement.
[02:31] Mateo Cruz: Also audit logs and retention — we can provide detailed request/response logs to your SIEM with configurable retention.
[02:40] Samir Patel: Need to confirm retention policies and whether logs include any raw PHI — we prefer redaction options.
[02:48] Priya Nair: We have redaction pipelines and the option to avoid storing full responses. We'll put the exact fields in the security doc.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: Pilot scope: 4-week pilot, ingesting a sample of 50k tokens/day, run NLU and extraction flows. Goal is validate quality, latency, and unit cost. Does that align?
[03:10] Rachel Kim: Sounds right, want to also validate reranking for triage prioritization.
[03:16] Priya Nair: Sure, we can include reranking. For the pilot we'll set up a dedicated model variant with quantization profile to reduce memory and cost, and run benchmarks.
[03:28] Alex Moreno: Which models are you recommending? We want open models if possible, but we might test Redwood-verified variants.
[03:35] Priya Nair: We'll propose a catalog: a smaller quantized open model for fast path and a higher-quality variant for fallback. Redwood has verified profiles showing throughput/latency tradeoffs. I'll attach that.
[03:48] Samir Patel: Network architecture — can you peer into our VPC? We have strict firewall rules.
[03:54] Jordan Lee: We support VPC peering for Private deployments and dedicated VPC options. For hosted APIs we can set up private connectivity via AWS PrivateLink as well. We'll follow-up with network diagrams.
[04:07] Leah Chen: Any PCI/HIPAA BAAs in place?
[04:11] Jordan Lee: We have a BAA for Private and Dedicated customers; hosted can be covered depending on purchase. We'll include legal contacts in the doc.
[04:22] Alex Moreno: On the measurement side, what telemetry will you expose? Token-level costs, per-route latency, p95/p99?
[04:29] Mateo Cruz: Yes, console provides token-level cost, per-model p50/p95/p99, tracing hooks and per-route dashboards. We'll demo that in the benchmark session.
[04:40] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, can you share representative request/response pairs? Preferably an S3 bucket or encrypted transfer.
[04:48] Alex Moreno: We'll prepare a 1k-sample set and an aggregate workload profile.
[04:53] Rachel Kim: Timeline — when can we start the pilot?
[04:57] Jordan Lee: If we get the security questionnaire answers and sample payloads this week, we can provision a pilot next week. Goal: pilot runs 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-23.
[05:08] Samir Patel: I'll try to get the questionnaire back by Monday. Network review might take a day or two after.
[05:15] Priya Nair: Great. I'll schedule a 60-minute benchmark session in the first week of the pilot to run latency and throughput tests, and demo the console.
[05:26] Leah Chen: For cost estimates, can you provide expected per-token costs across the two model variants?
[05:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll send a detailed pricing sheet showing per-token estimates, the impact of batching and caching, and dedicated commit options that reduce unit cost.
[05:40] Alex Moreno: Any known accuracy regressions with quantized models for extraction tasks?
[05:45] Priya Nair: There's usually a small delta; part of the pilot is running evals on your labeled set. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and monitor regressions tied to evals.
[05:58] Rachel Kim: Ok good. Sweat test question — if we hit a surge, what's the graceful degradation path?
[06:05] Priya Nair: We have smart routing and fallback policies. We can route to a cheaper hosted variant or throttle non-critical routes. For Dedicated customers we also support temporary burst capacity.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: Let's capture action items and owners — Mateo, you'll run the onboarding checklist. Priya, benchmark testing. Samir, security Q. Jordan, pricing and contract.
[06:31] Mateo Cruz: I'll set up the weekly sync invite and the onboarding doc in Confluence.
[06:36] Samir Patel: Note: we may need on-prem option long term. For pilot we'll try VPC peering.
[06:42] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll include Private deployment options in the docs.
[06:46] Rachel Kim: Anything else?
[06:48] Jordan Lee: That's it — quick recap: Jordan to send security and pricing docs, Priya to schedule/perform benchmarks, Mateo to run onboarding cadence, Seabright to deliver payloads and questionnaire.
[07:00] Rachel Kim: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:04] Jordan Lee: Thanks all — see you in the benchmark session.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts: occasional filler words, truncated tech acronyms transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' as 'kay vee cache'), minor speaker label mismatches possible.
